actions.action: Poke a white spot with a swab or toothpick to confirm it is a soft mealybug
Look for honeydew, ants, yellowing or stunted growth
Dab each mealybug with a cotton swab dipped in 70% isopropyl alcohol
Check the roots for white cottony clumps (root mealybugs) while repotting
Gently rinse roots and stems under lukewarm water
Discard the old soil in a sealed bag
Clean the pot with soapy water or dilute bleach
Test insecticidal soap or neem oil on a small area first
Spray insecticidal soap or neem oil on stems and leaf undersides, repeated weekly for 4-6 weeks
Optionally apply a systemic soil insecticide if the plant won't be eaten
Set up gloves and newspaper or an outdoor spot for the repotting work

reason: The answer names mealybugs as the main diagnosis and makes dabbing with 70% alcohol a core early step, matching the fix that worked, while its extra repotting and spraying steps are excessive but not harmful.
